correctness.rationale: Because the center is the derived line, write F(z)=λz and F(v)=Av+c(v)z. Bracket preservation gives ω(Av,Aw)=λω(v,w), and idempotence gives A²=A, λ²=λ and cA+λc=c. Over any field λ is 0 or 1. At λ=1, nondegeneracy forces A injective, hence the identity by idempotence, and then c=0. At λ=0, A is a projection onto an isotropic U and c=ηA is determined by its restriction η to U; conversely these data suffice. Thus the image is the specified graph, has rank r=dim U≤n, and meets the center trivially. Every r≤n occurs by selecting vectors from a symplectic basis. Counting ordered isotropic bases gives q^(2n−j)−q^j extensions at stage j; divide by the ordered-basis count to obtain I_(n,r). Graphs over each U are distinct for distinct η, and a fixed graph leaves exactly the choice of a complement to U in V, parametrized by Hom(V/U,U). This verifies the rank formula, the per-image multiplicity, the zero and full-rank cases, and both example polynomials. No division by 2 is used. A fresh replay enumerated all 512 binary 3×3 matrices, tested the bracket on basis pairs and F²=F, and counted spans of the columns: 64 Lie endomorphisms, with retraction counts (1,12,0,1) by rank and two retractions for each of six rank-one images. This is a bounded check, not the unbounded proof. The bound VERIFICATION.md, REVIEW.md and artifacts/check_heisenberg.py were inspected; the uploaded script was not executed.
